name: Taffeta-Storm
specific_features: Cloud bands with iridescent sheen resembling taffeta fabric
Persistent anticyclone producing visible lightning from orbit
description: Taffeta-Storm is a massive gas giant whose cloud bands display a distinctive iridescent quality, shifting between metallic blues, greens, and purples as they catch light from the system's twin stars at varying angles. The effect is caused by ammonia crystal formations in the upper atmosphere that refract light in ways unique to this planet's specific chemical composition, creating a surface that ripples and shimmers like taffeta fabric in motion. The beauty is entirely superficial, concealing one of the most violent atmospheric systems ever documented.

The planet's twin-star system creates complex heating patterns that drive atmospheric winds exceeding two thousand kilometers per hour in the mid-latitudes. These supersonic winds shear against slower-moving equatorial bands, generating storms of staggering intensity. Lightning discharges span thousands of kilometers, visible from neighboring planets during opposition. The ammonia thunderstorm layer, approximately three hundred kilometers below the cloud tops, produces electromagnetic pulses powerful enough to damage unshielded electronics at considerable distance.

Deep atmosphere models predict that the extreme pressures within Taffeta-Storm compress carbon into diamond, which precipitates downward through the hydrogen-helium mixture as a continuous rain of gemstones. These diamonds, accumulating over billions of years, may form a solid layer thousands of kilometers thick within the planet's interior. The theoretical diamond reserves exceed the total mass of many terrestrial planets, an incomprehensible wealth locked behind equally incomprehensible pressures.

Taffeta-Storm's helium-3 reserves make it a strategic asset despite its hostile nature, and a network of automated scoop-ships operates in the relatively calm upper atmosphere during predictable weather windows. Losses average twelve percent per operational cycle, an acceptable rate given the value of the extracted fuel. Proposals to attempt deep-atmosphere diamond mining have been universally dismissed as suicidal with current technology. The planet continues its violent, beautiful dance, its taffeta clouds hiding treasures that may never be reached, its storms raging with an energy that dwarfs anything human civilization has ever produced.
